chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in all Achaia: VerseEnd Verse2 Grace be to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse3 Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort, VerseEnd Verse4 who comforts us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them who are in any trouble by the comfort by which we ourselves are comforted of God. VerseEnd Verse5 For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also abounds by Christ. VerseEnd

Verse6 And whether we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer; or whether we are comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation. VerseEnd Verse7 And our hope of you is steadfast, knowing that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation. VerseEnd Verse8 For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia — that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life. VerseEnd Verse9 But we had the sentence of death in ourselves that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead, VerseEnd Verse10 who delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver, in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us. VerseEnd Verse11 You also helping together by prayer for us, that, for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many people, thanks may be given by many on our behalf. VerseEnd

Verse12 For our rejoicing is this: the testimony of our conscience that in simplicity and godly sincerity — not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God — we have had our conduct reversed in the world, and more abundantly toward you. VerseEnd Verse13 For we write no other things unto you than what you read or acknowledge, and I trust you shall acknowledge even to the end, VerseEnd Verse14 as also you have acknowledged us in part — that we are your rejoicing, even as you also are ours, in the day of the Lord Jesus. VerseEnd Verse15 And in this confidence I was determined to come unto you before, that you might have a second benefit, VerseEnd Verse16 and to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judea. VerseEnd

Verse17 When I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea, yea, and nay, nay? VerseEnd Verse18 But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay, VerseEnd Verse19 for the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea; VerseEnd Verse20 for all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him amen, unto the glory of God by us. VerseEnd Verse21 Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, is God, VerseEnd Verse22 who has also sealed us and given the earnest payment of the spirit in our hearts. VerseEnd

Verse23 Moreover, I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth. VerseEnd Verse24 Not that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy, for by faith you stand. VerseEnd LEChapter2 Verse1 But I determined this with myself: that I would not come again to you in heaviness; VerseEnd Verse2 for if I make you sorry, who is he then that makes me glad but the same who is made sorry by me? VerseEnd Verse3 And I wrote this same unto you, lest when I came I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice, having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all. VerseEnd Verse4 For out of much affliction and anguish of heart, I wrote unto you with many tears — not that you should be grieved, but that you might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you. VerseEnd

Verse5 But if any have caused grief, he has not grieved me but in part, that I may not burden you all. VerseEnd Verse6 Sufficient to such a man is this punishment which was inflicted of many, VerseEnd Verse7 so that contrariwise you ought rather to forgive him and comfort him, lest perhaps such an one should be swallowed up with too much sorrow. VerseEnd Verse8 Wherefore, I implore you that you would confirm your love toward him. VerseEnd

Verse9 For to this end also did I write: that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things. VerseEnd Verse10 To whom you forgive anything, I forgive also. For if I forgave anything, to whom I forgave it, for your sakes I forgave it in the person of Christ, VerseEnd Verse11 lest Satan should get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. VerseEnd

Verse12 Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christ’s gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord, VerseEnd Verse13 I had no rest in my spirit because I found not Titus my brother. But taking my leave of them, I went from there into Macedonia. VerseEnd Verse14 Now thanks be unto God, who always causes us to triumph in Christ and makes manifest the savor of his knowledge by us in every place; VerseEnd Verse15 for we are unto God a sweet savor of Christ, in them that are saved and in them that perish VerseEnd — Verse16 to the one we are the savor of death unto death, and to the other, the savor of life unto life.

And who is sufficient for these things? VerseEnd Verse17 For we are not as many who corrupt the word of God, but as of sincerity. But as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ. VerseEnd LEChapter3 Verse1 Do we begin again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as some others, epistles of commendation to you? Or letters of commendation from you? VerseEnd Verse2 You are our epistle, written in our hearts, known and read of all men, VerseEnd Verse3 forasmuch as you are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us — written not with ink but with the spirit of the living God, not in tablets of stone but in fleshy tablets of the heart. VerseEnd Verse4 And such trust have we through Christ toward God. VerseEnd Verse5 Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves, but our sufficiency is of God, VerseEnd Verse6 who also has made us able ministers of the new covenant — not of the letter, but of the spirit; for the letter kills, but the spirit gives life. VerseEnd

Verse7 But if the ministration of death (written and engraved in stones) was glorious — so that the children of Israel could not steadfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance, which glory was to be done away VerseEnd — Verse8 how shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious? VerseEnd Verse9 For if the ministration of condemnation is glory, much more does the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory. VerseEnd Verse10 For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excels; VerseEnd Verse11 for if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remains is glorious. VerseEnd

Verse12 Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech, VerseEnd Verse13 and not as Moses, who put a veil over his face that the children of Israel could not steadfastly look to the end of that which is abolished. VerseEnd Verse14 But their minds were blinded, for until this day remains the same veil, untaken away in the reading of the old covenant, which veil is done away in Christ; VerseEnd Verse15 but even unto this day, when Moses is read, the veil is upon their heart. VerseEnd Verse16 Nevertheless, when their heart shall turn to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away. VerseEnd Verse17 Now the Lord is that Spirit, and where the spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. VerseEnd Verse18 But we all, with open face beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image, from glory to glory, even as by the spirit of the Lord. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 Therefore, seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not, VerseEnd Verse2 but have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness nor handling the word of God deceitfully, but by manifestation of the truth, commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God. VerseEnd Verse3 But if our gospel is hidden, it is hidden to them that are lost, VerseEnd Verse4 in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of them who believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ (who is the image of God) should shine unto them. VerseEnd Verse5 For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord, and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. VerseEnd

Verse6 For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, has shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse7 But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellence of the power may be of God and not of us. VerseEnd Verse8 We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; VerseEnd Verse9 persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed; VerseEnd Verse10 always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body. VerseEnd Verse11 For we who live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh. VerseEnd Verse12 So then it works death unto us, but life unto you. VerseEnd

Verse13 We having the same spirit of faith according as it is written: I believed, and therefore have I spoken. We also believe and therefore speak, VerseEnd Verse14 knowing that he who raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise us up also by Jesus, and shall present us with you; VerseEnd Verse15 for we bear all things for your sakes, that the abundant grace might, through the thanksgiving of many, return to the glory of God, VerseEnd Verse16 for which cause we faint not. But though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day; VerseEnd Verse17 for our light affliction (which is but for a moment) works for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory, VerseEnd Verse18 while we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen; for the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal. VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the Heavens. VerseEnd Verse2 For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from Heaven, VerseEnd Verse3 that being clothed we shall not be found naked; VerseEnd Verse4 for we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened — not that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life. VerseEnd Verse5 Now he that has wrought us for the selfsame thing is God, who also has given unto us the earnest payment of the spirit; VerseEnd Verse6 therefore, we are always confident, knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord VerseEnd (Verse7 for we walk by faith, not by sight) VerseEnd. Verse8 We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body and to be present with the Lord. VerseEnd

Verse9 Wherefore, we labor that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him. VerseEnd Verse10 For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that everyone may receive a reward of the deeds done in the body — things according to what he has done, whether good or bad. VerseEnd

Verse11 Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men. But we are made manifest unto God, and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences; VerseEnd Verse12 for we commend not ourselves again unto you, but give you opportunity to glory on our behalf, that you may have somewhat to answer them who glory in appearance and not in heart. VerseEnd Verse13 For we bear record that we are not beside ourselves. For whether we glory, it is to God, or whether we are sober, it is for your sakes. VerseEnd Verse14 For the love of Christ constrains us because we thus judge: that if one died for all, then are all dead, VerseEnd Verse15 and that he died for all, that they who live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him who died for them and rose again. VerseEnd

Verse16 Wherefore, henceforth live we no more after the flesh. Yea, though we once lived after the flesh, yet since we have known Christ, now henceforth live we no more after the flesh. VerseEnd Verse17 Therefore, if any man live in Christ, he is a new creature (old things are passed away; behold, all things have become new) VerseEnd, Verse18 and receives all the things of God, who has reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and has given to us the ministry of reconciliation VerseEnd — Verse19 namely that God is, in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them — and has committed unto us the word of reconciliation. VerseEnd

Verse20 Now then we are ambassadors for Christ as though God did implore you by us. We pray you in Christ’s stead: be reconciled to God; VerseEnd Verse21 for he has made him to be sin, who knew no sin, for us, that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. VerseEnd

LEChapter6 Verse1 We then, as workers together with Christ, implore you also that you receive not the grace of God in vain VerseEnd (Verse2 for he says, I have heard you in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succored you. Behold now is the accepted time, behold now is the day of salvation) VerseEnd, Verse3 giving no offense in anything (that the ministry be not blamed) VerseEnd, Verse4 but in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God: in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, VerseEnd Verse5 in stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labors, in sleeplessness, in fastings, VerseEnd Verse6 by pureness, by knowledge, by long-suffering, by kindness, by the holy ghost, by love unfeigned, VerseEnd Verse7 by the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left, VerseEnd Verse8 by honor and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true; VerseEnd Verse9 as unknown, and yet well-known; as dying, and behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed; VerseEnd Verse10 as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things. VerseEnd

Verse11 O you Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged, VerseEnd Verse12 you are not restrained in us; but you are restrained in your own affections. VerseEnd Verse13 Now for a recompense in the same (I speak as unto my children), you also be enlarged. VerseEnd Verse14 Be not unequally yoked together with unbelievers, for what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? And what communion has light with darkness? VerseEnd Verse15 And what concord has Christ with Belial? Or what part has he that believes with an unbeliever? VerseEnd Verse16 And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God, as God has said: I will dwell in them and walk in them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. VerseEnd Verse17 Wherefore, come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing, and I will receive you VerseEnd Verse18 and will be a Father unto you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty. VerseEnd
LEChapter7 Verse1 Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God. VerseEnd

Verse2 Receive us. We have wronged no man. We have corrupted no man. We have defrauded no man. VerseEnd Verse3 I speak not this to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die and live with you. VerseEnd Verse4 Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying of you. I am filled with comfort. I am exceedingly joyful in all our tribulation. VerseEnd

Verse5 For when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side: outside were fightings; within were fears. VerseEnd Verse6 Nevertheless, God, who comforts those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus VerseEnd — Verse7 and not by his coming only, but by the consolation with which he was comforted in you (when he told us your earnest desire, your mourning, your fervent mind toward me), so that I rejoiced the more. VerseEnd Verse8 For though I made you sorry with a letter, I do not regret it — though I did regret. For I perceive that the same epistle has made you sorry, though it was but for a season. VerseEnd Verse9 Now I rejoice — not that you were made sorry, but that you sorrowed to repentance; for you were made sorry after a godly manner, that you might receive damage by us in nothing. VerseEnd Verse10 For godly sorrow works repentance to salvation, not to be repented of, but the sorrow of the world works death. VerseEnd Verse11 For behold, this selfsame thing (that you sorrowed after a godly sort), what concern it wrought in you — yea, what clearing of yourselves, yea, what indignation, yea, what fear, yea, what vehement desire, yea, what zeal, yea, what revenge. In all things you have proved yourselves to be clear in this matter. VerseEnd

Verse12 Wherefore, though I wrote unto you, I did it not for his cause that had done the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered wrong, but that our care for you in the sight of God might appear unto you. VerseEnd Verse13 Therefore, we were comforted in your comfort, yea, and exceedingly the more rejoiced we for the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by you all. VerseEnd Verse14 For if I have boasted anything to him of you, I am not ashamed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, even so our boasting which I made before Titus is found a truth. VerseEnd Verse15 And his inward affection is more abundant toward you while he remembers the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you received him. VerseEnd Verse16 I rejoice therefore that I have confidence in you in all things. VerseEnd

LEChapter8 Verse1 Moreover, brethren, we would have you to know of the grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia VerseEnd — Verse2 that in a great trial of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality. VerseEnd Verse3 For to their power I bear record, yea, and beyond their power they were willing of themselves, VerseEnd Verse4 asking us with much entreaty that we would receive the gift and take upon us the fellowship of the ministering to the saints. VerseEnd Verse5 And this they did, not as we required, but first gave their own selves to the Lord, and unto us by the will of God, VerseEnd Verse6 insomuch that we desired of Titus that as he had begun, so he would also finish in you the same grace also. VerseEnd Verse7 Therefore, as you abound in every thing — in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all diligence, and in your love to us — see that you abound in this grace also. VerseEnd Verse8 I speak not by commandment, but by occasion of the earnestness of others and to prove the sincerity of your love. VerseEnd

Verse9 For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might be rich. VerseEnd Verse10 And herein I give my advice, for this is expedient for you who have begun before — not only to do, but also to be desirous a year ago. VerseEnd Verse11 Now therefore perform the doing of it, that as there was a readiness to will, so there may be a performance also out of that which you have; VerseEnd Verse12 for if there is first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man has, and not according to that he has not. VerseEnd Verse13 For I mean not that other men be eased and you burdened, VerseEnd Verse14 but by an equality — that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their lack, that their abundance also may be a supply for your lack, that there may be equality, VerseEnd Verse15 as it is written: He that had gathered much had nothing over, and he that had gathered little had no lack. VerseEnd

Verse16 But thanks be to God, who put the same earnest care into the heart of Titus for you; VerseEnd Verse17 for indeed he accepted the exhortation, but being more forward, of his own accord he went unto you. VerseEnd Verse18 And we have sent with him the brother whose praise is in the gospel throughout all the churches, VerseEnd Verse19 and not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us, with this grace which is administered by us, to the glory of the same Lord and declaring of your ready mind, VerseEnd Verse20 avoiding this — that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us, VerseEnd Verse21 providing for honest things not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men. VerseEnd Verse22 And we have sent with them our brother whom we have proved diligent in many things, but now much more diligent. Therefore, we send him unto you in consequence of the great confidence which we have in you — that you will receive the things concerning you to the glory of Christ, VerseEnd Verse23 whether we send by the hand of Titus (my partner and fellow laborer) or our brethren (the messengers of the churches) VerseEnd. Verse24 Wherefore, show to them, and before the churches, the proof of your love and of our boasting on your behalf. VerseEnd

LEChapter9 Verse1 For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you; VerseEnd Verse2 for I know the readiness of your mind, for which I boast of you to them of Macedonia — that Achaia was ready a year ago; and your zeal has provoked very many. VerseEnd Verse3 Yet have I sent the brethren, lest our boasting of you should be in vain in this behalf, that as I said, you may be ready; VerseEnd Verse4 lest if they of Macedonia come with me and find you unprepared, we (that we say, not you) should be ashamed in this same confident boasting. VerseEnd Verse5 Therefore, I thought it necessary to exhort the brethren that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your bounty whereof you had notice before, that the same might be ready as a matter of bounty and not as of covetousness. VerseEnd

Verse6 But this I say: he who sows sparingly shall reap also sparingly, and he who sows bountifully shall reap also bountifully VerseEnd — Verse7 every man according as he purposes in his heart; so let him give not grudgingly or of necessity, for God VerseEnd Verse8 loves a cheerful giver. And God is able to make all grace abound toward you, that you, always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work, VerseEnd Verse9 as it is written: He has dispersed abroad, he has given to the poor, his righteousness remains for ever. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now he that ministers seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness VerseEnd — Verse11 being enriched in everything to all bountifulness — which causes, through us, thanksgiving to God. VerseEnd Verse12 For the administration of this service not only supplies the lack of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God, VerseEnd Verse13 while by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection unto the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal distribution unto them and unto VerseEnd Verse14 all men, and by their prayer for you, who long after you for the exceeding grace of God in you. VerseEnd Verse15 Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift. VerseEnd

LEChapter10 Verse1 Now I, Paul, myself implore you (by the meekness and gentleness of Christ), who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you; VerseEnd Verse2 but I implore you that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence with which I think to be bold against some who think of us as if we walked according to the flesh. VerseEnd Verse3 For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh, VerseEnd Verse4 for the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God, to the pulling down of strong holds, VerseEnd Verse5 casting down imaginations and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ, VerseEnd Verse6 and having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience when your obedience is fulfilled. VerseEnd

Verse7 Do you look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trust to himself that he is Christ’s, let him of himself think this again: that as he is Christ’s, even so are we Christ’s. VerseEnd Verse8 For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord has given us for edification and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed, VerseEnd Verse9 that I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters. VerseEnd Verse10 For his letters (say they) are weighty and powerful, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible. VerseEnd Verse11 Let such an one think this: that such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such will we also be in deed when we are present. VerseEnd

Verse12 For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves; but they, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise. VerseEnd Verse13 But we will not boast of things outside our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God has distributed to us, a measure to reach even unto you. VerseEnd Verse14 For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure (as though we reached not unto you), for we have come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ, VerseEnd Verse15 not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other men’s labors, but having hope (when your faith is increased) that we shall be enlarged by you (according to our rule) abundantly, VerseEnd Verse16 to preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another man’s line of things made ready to our hand. VerseEnd Verse17 But he that glories, let him glory in the Lord, VerseEnd Verse18 for not he that commends himself is approved, but whom the Lord commends. VerseEnd

LEChapter11 Verse1 Would to God you could bear with me a little in my folly — and indeed, bear with me. VerseEnd Verse2 For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy, for I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. VerseEnd Verse3 But I fear, lest by any means as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtlety, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ. VerseEnd Verse4 For if he that comes preach another Jesus whom we have not preached, or if you receive another spirit which you have not received, or another gospel which you have not accepted, you might well bear with me. VerseEnd Verse5 For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles, VerseEnd Verse6 but though I am unrefined in speech — yet not in knowledge. But we have been thoroughly made manifest among you in all things. VerseEnd

Verse7 Have I committed an offense in abasing myself that you might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God freely? VerseEnd Verse8 I robbed other churches, taking wages of them to do you service. VerseEnd Verse9 And when I was present with you and lacked, I was burdensome to no man; for that which was lacking to me, the brethren who came from Macedonia supplied. And in all things I have kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself. VerseEnd Verse10 As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia. VerseEnd Verse11 Why? Because I love you not? God knows. VerseEnd

Verse12 But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off opportunity from them who desire opportunity that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we; VerseEnd Verse13 for such are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ VerseEnd — Verse14 and no marvel, for Satan himself disguises as an angel of light. VerseEnd Verse15 Therefore, it is no great thing if his ministers also are disguised as the ministers of righteousness, whose end shall be according to their works. VerseEnd

Verse16 I say again, let no man think me a fool. If otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little. VerseEnd Verse17 That which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as if it were foolishly in this confidence of boasting. VerseEnd Verse18 Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also. VerseEnd Verse19 For you suffer fools gladly, seeing you yourselves are wise; VerseEnd Verse20 for you suffer if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take of you, if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face. VerseEnd Verse21 I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak.

Nevertheless, in whatever any is bold (I speak foolishly), I am bold also. VerseEnd Verse22 Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? So am I. VerseEnd Verse23 Are they ministers of Christ? — I speak as a fool — so am I: in labors more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft. VerseEnd Verse24 Of the Jews, five times received I forty stripes save one; VerseEnd Verse25 three times was I beaten with rods; once was I stoned; three times I suffered shipwreck; a night and a day I have been in the deep; VerseEnd Verse26 in journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by my own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren; VerseEnd Verse27 in weariness and labor, in sleeplessness often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness; VerseEnd Verse28 beside those things that are outside, that which comes upon me daily — the care of all the churches. VerseEnd Verse29 Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is offended, and I anger not? VerseEnd

Verse30 If I must glory, I will glory of the things which concern my infirmities. VerseEnd Verse31 The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed for ever, knows that I lie not. VerseEnd Verse32 In Damascus, the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me, VerseEnd Verse33 and through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall and escaped his hands. VerseEnd

LEChapter12 Verse1 It is not expedient for me doubtless to glory. I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse2 I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I cannot tell, or whether out of the body, I cannot tell; God knows), such an one caught up to the third Heaven. VerseEnd Verse3 And I knew such a man (whether in the body or out of the body, I cannot tell; God knows) VerseEnd, Verse4 that he was caught up into paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter. VerseEnd Verse5 Of such an one will I glory.

Yet of myself I will not glory, but in my infirmities; VerseEnd Verse6 for though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool, for I will say the truth; but now I refrain, lest any man should think of me above that which he sees of me or that he hears of me. VerseEnd

Verse7 And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure. VerseEnd Verse8 For this thing, I implored the Lord three times that it might depart from me. VerseEnd Verse9 And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for you; for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. VerseEnd Verse10 Therefore, I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ’s sake; for when I am weak, then am I strong. VerseEnd

Verse11 I have become a fool in glorying. You have compelled me, for I ought to have been commended of you, for in nothing am I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I am nothing. VerseEnd Verse12 Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds. VerseEnd Verse13 For what is it wherein you were inferior to other churches, except it be that I myself was not burdensome to you? Forgive me this wrong. VerseEnd

Verse14 Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be burdensome to you; for I seek not yours, but you. For the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children. VerseEnd Verse15 And I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I am loved. VerseEnd Verse16 But be it so. I did not burden you. Nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile. VerseEnd Verse17 Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent unto you? VerseEnd Verse18 I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not walk in the same steps? VerseEnd

Verse19 Again, do you think that we excuse ourselves unto you? We speak before God in Christ. But we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edifying. VerseEnd Verse20 For I fear lest when I come, I shall not find you such as I wish, and that I shall be found unto you such as you wish not; lest there should be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults; VerseEnd Verse21 and lest when I come again, my God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many who have sinned already and have not repented of the uncleanness, and fornication, and lasciviousness which they have committed. VerseEnd

LEChapter13 Verse1 This is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established. VerseEnd Verse2 I told you before, and foretell you as if I were present the second time, and being absent now, I write to them who before now have sinned, and to all other, that if I come again, I will not spare, VerseEnd Verse3 since you seek a proof of Christ speaking in me — who toward you is not weak, but is mighty in you; VerseEnd Verse4 for though he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you. VerseEnd

Verse5 Examine yourselves, whether you are in the faith; prove your own selves. Do you not know your own selves that Jesus Christ is in you, except you are reprobates? VerseEnd Verse6 But I trust that you shall know that we are not reprobates. VerseEnd Verse7 Now I pray to God that you do no evil — not that we should appear approved, but that you should do that which is good, though we are as reprobates. VerseEnd Verse8 For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth. VerseEnd Verse9 For we are glad when we are weak and you are strong. And this also we wish: even your perfection. VerseEnd Verse10 Therefore, I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness — according to the power which the Lord has given me to edification, and not to destruction. VerseEnd

Verse11 Finally brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace shall be with you. VerseEnd Verse12 Greet one another with a holy salutation. VerseEnd Verse13 All the saints salute you. VerseEnd Verse14 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the holy ghost be with you all. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The second epistle to the Corinthians was written from Philippi of Macedonia by Titus and Lucas.
